arms/step-guard-asymmetry: Difference 7: only compare_guarded's guarded arm gets a step guard, and the cell 11 and cell 12 guarded runs get none at all -- Quote verified verbatim at builder/lab/notebooks/w6-lab.ipynb:1904, and the mechanical observation is true: guarded_triage() passes over_token_cap as step_guard (line 1905) while the undefended run at line 1959 passes nothing. But every inferential step built on that is contradicted by the file.

(1) The "three tables" do not exist. Grepping the literal column label finds "guarded" as a table column in exactly two places: line 1580 (cell 11) and line 2022 (cell 16). Cell 12's placement table header, line 1652, is: "    \"    print(f\\\"{'id':<6}{'placement':<20}{'verdict':<12}{'conf':<8}fence reaches it\\\")\\n\"," — there is no "guarded" column in it at all. The finding invents one to reach the number three.

(2) The cell 11 table already states, in its own output, exactly what the finding says is concealed. Lines 1590-1591: "    \"    print(\\\"Read the 013 row. The two columns are the same agent on the same\\\")\\n\"," and "    \"    print(\\\"message. The fence is the only thing that changed.\\\")\\n\"," — the student is told in plain words that the guarded column there is the fence and nothing else.

(3) The step guard is not a stealth "seventh difference"; it is control 4, announced on the line immediately above the quoted call. Line 1903: "    \"    # Control 4, the token cap, goes in as the loop's step guard.\\n\"," and again in the reading, builder/content/pages/w6-content.md:75: "**4. The per-run token cap.** ... `over_token_cap()` reports when a run passes it, and `guarded_triage()` hands that check to your week 5 loop as its step guard." Cell 16's columns are "no guard" and "guarded" (line 2022), so all four controls differing between the arms is the comparison's purpose, not a leak in it.

(4) The claim that "the cell 11 table is the one the reading and the wrap-up quote" is false. The reading points at cell 16 for the guarded-vs-undefended comparison — builder/content/pages/w6-content.md:115: "The lab runs eleven emails twice, undefended and guarded, and prints the comparison in cell 16." The wrap-up's only 013/024 line is builder/content/pages/w6-wrap-up.md:23: "- You ran email 013 and its clean twin 024 with no defenses." — the cell 6/7 plain runs, not the cell 11 guarded table. Neither page cites cell 11's table as evidence of four controls working.

The only residue worth the parent's attention is much narrower and was not what was reported: the cell 6 header comment at line 1227-1228 says "Both paths this week use run_triage(), so\n# the only thing that changes between them is the prompt." — which is loose once line 1905 also hands over a step_guard. That is a one-sentence comment overstatement in a pre-written cell the student does not edit, corrected 670 lines later by line 1903's own comment, and nothing a student sees or is graded on turns on it.

arms/token-cap-cannot-fire: over_token_cap() cannot end a run at the shipped cap: the loop's ceiling before the last step is 3072 written tokens against a cap of 4000 -- Quote verified verbatim at /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/lab/notebooks/w6-lab.ipynb:2066. Refuted on four independent grounds.

1. The surrounding text already says the thing the finding says is concealed. The very same comment block continues at lines 2067-2070: "That is the design. A cap you meet every day is a budget, not a cap. It is / there for the run that will not settle, and week 5 showed you what one of / those costs. This cell drops the cap to 5 for one run, so the control is / visible on your own screen, and then puts it back." Two other student-facing files repeat it plainly: /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/content/pages/w6-content.md:77 — "One honest word about the cap. A normal run here costs far less than 4000, so it won't fire on its own. Cell 17 lowers it on purpose, and that's where you watch it work." — and /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/content/assignments/w6-lab.md:20 — "11. Run cell 17. It lowers the token cap on purpose so you watch the cap fire. A normal run here spends far less than 4000." The artifact never claims the cap fires on its own in this lab; it says the opposite three times.

2. The finding's mechanism analysis is factually wrong twice. (a) "The guard is consulted only inside run_loop at line 1197" is false. over_token_cap() is called a second time in guarded_triage at line 1925 — "    if over_token_cap():\n" (w6-lab.ipynb:1925) — after run_triage returns, and that is the call site producing the student-visible escalate_reason "token_cap" column and the exported JSON field, not the in-loop guard. (b) "The control is unreachable by arithmetic, not by luck" is false and self-contradicting: the finding itself computes 4 x 1024 = 4096 > 4000. It also missed the closing call — run_triage does "    answer = extract_json(ask_model(closing))\n" (w6-lab.ipynb:1257) with ask_model's default "def ask_model(prompt, max_tokens=512, temperature=0.2):\n" (w6-lab.ipynb:524), and send_request records every call's usage, so the ceiling at the line-1925 check is 4x1024+512 = 4608, comfortably above 4000. The cap is unreachable by luck, not by arithmetic — the exact inverse of the claim.

3. The claim in the quote is measured true, not unmeasured hand-waving. /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/docs/week6-measurement/baseline-granite-3b-8.json records tokens_written per run across the corpus in the 133-288 range (e.g. runs[0] guarded 217, plain 274; runs[3] guarded 236; runs[10] plain 288) against a 4000 cap, with conditions/token_cap False on every row. "No triage in this lab comes near it" is a reported measurement.

4. Severity is inflated, and the residual is already a logged, deliberated decision. Nothing a student sees or is graded on depends on the cap firing at 4000: cell 17 is pre-written and demonstrates the control by lowering it to 5, cell 16 (the screenshot cell) is unaffected, and exam Q30 in builder/content/quizzes/exam-parts/CLO4.yaml asks only what TOKEN_CAP_PER_RUN counts. The one genuine kernel — that written tokens are not the quantity that grows on a runaway loop — is already carried openly in /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/docs/lab-fix-log.md:920-924: "**The SOC review says two of the four taught controls measure the wrong / thing.** `over_token_cap()` reads `RUN_USAGE[\"answer\"]`, but completion tokens / do not grow across a loop — prompt history does, which week 5 teaches / correctly. ... Forcing either to fire would hide the defect rather than fix it." And cell 17 discloses the same distinction to the student directly, printing that the cap reads the written number and "No cap in this lab reads it" of the total. Not blocking, not a hidden dead control.

These samples found a different number:\")\n" (line 1821). A correct function prints "    print(\"Good. All three samples found the number of problems expected.\")\n" (line 1820). Stub, wrong, and correct are three different screens.

2. TODO 2's own instructions point at it. Lab notebook line 1746: "# How to tell it worked: run the next cell. It feeds your function three\n", and line 1747: "# made-up answers. The first has to come back with three problems. The other\n". The assignment repeats it at /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/content/assignments/w6-lab.md:16.

3. The very text the finding cites as evidence of the defect is the notebook redirecting the student to that instrument. Solution lines 2023-2024: "    print(\"   message never showed. 4. The swallow is disclosed, not hidden. Lab notebook line 1818: "    print(\"Nothing is broken. The runs below treat every answer as clean.\")\n", and the assignment's warning callout at w6-lab.md:31: "`check_against_facts()` hands back a list. An empty list means it found nothing wrong. Return `True` or `None` instead and `guarded_triage()` can't read it."

The rubric half of the finding is accurate but is not a week 6 defect: it is the stated course-wide grading policy. /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/content/rubrics/w6-lab.yaml carries "# NOTHING HERE NEEDS THE STUDENT'S NOTEBOOK. Every level is decided from the" (line 72), and the identical header sits in w4-lab.yaml:53, w5-lab.yaml:56 and w7-lab.yaml:77. The assignment says it outright at w6-lab.md:39: "Nothing here is graded by running your notebook. The three items you turn in carry all of it." No week's rubric reads any student function's return value, so "no criterion reads problems" describes the whole course's artifact-based grading, not a week 6 flaw, and week 6 does not depend on it being otherwise.

The one true residue is narrow and minor: a student who leaves TODO 2 blank can still reach 100 points, because the three graded artifacts do not distinguish an empty problems list produced by a correct check from one produced by the stub. That is a consequence of the declared policy rather than a hole in week 6, and it costs the student the cell 15 confirmation either way.

gradeable/fence-record-earned-without-todo1: Criterion 3's fence-record clause is satisfied by a student who never wrote build_guarded_prompt() -- Quote verified verbatim at builder/content/rubrics/w6-lab.yaml:147-150 (line 149 = "name a payload placement and five read none. The fence record for"). The mechanism is also real: builder/lab/notebooks/w6-lab.ipynb:1427-1428 is exactly "    if not isinstance(prompt_text, str):" / "        prompt_text = \"\"", fence_check() returns all four keys unconditionally (1435-1438), the export cell calls it on whatever build_guarded_prompt() returned (2119-2121), and guarded_triage() falls back instead of raising ("    else:\n        prompt_text = loop_prompt(parsed)", 1899-1900). So a student who leaves TODO 1 as `pass` does export guard_fence_check with -1/-1/0/len.

The finding is refuted on its central premise, not its mechanism. It asserts the artifact claims a present fence record is evidence of a built fence, and that this clause is "the one clause carrying objective 6.1 into a graded artifact." The artifact says the opposite, nine lines above the quoted level, in the same criterion's long_description (w6-lab.yaml:140-142): "record for email 013 is present. This criterion is a week expectation, / not a course outcome: it scores what the exported file holds, not how / good the run was. CLO4 is carried by criterion 2." The rubric header states the same at lines 46-50 ("Criteria 1 and 3 carry no Outcome link... Criterion 3 checks what the exported file contains rather than how good the run was"). And the week 6 spec records the exact gap as a deliberate, disclosed design decision (builder/docs/phase1-blueprint/week-06-spec.md:158-162): "One limit, stated plainly rather than smoothed over. No rubric criterion scores / the quality of the fenced prompt on its own. Criterion 3 checks only that the / fence record is in the file... So 6.1 is graded through its / effect, not on its own." This is the refutation ground "the surrounding text already says the thing the finding says is missing."

Two further corrections. (1) The notebook does not let a fence-less student through silently: cell 11 prints "build_guarded_prompt() is not written yet. It gave back:" and skips the guarded run entirely, cell 12 prints "build_guarded_prompt() is not written yet, so there is no guarded" and makes no model call, and guarded_triage's own comment (1896-1897) documents the fallback as intentional so the eleven-email cell still runs. (2) The assignment page does not, as the finding says, tell the student to check the indices; builder/content/assignments/w6-lab.md:22 says only "the fence record for email 013 is there."

What survives is smaller than "major" and belongs to criterion 2, not the quoted clause: because guarded_triage falls back to loop_prompt(), the spec's stated mitigation that "6.1 is graded through its effect" is weaker than the spec asserts, since the other three controls still produce guarded verdicts with no fence. That is a defensible tightening of criterion 3's Full level (require body_start_index != -1, or fenced_body_chars >= email_body_chars, the test the notebook itself runs at 1562-1565), but it does not make criterion 3 defective as authored, and it costs 20 points on an explicitly non-outcome completeness criterion after the student has ignored two loud in-notebook blockers.

evidence/false-escalation-omitted-from-decision: granite-8b's guarded arm escalates 114 of 120 benign decoy runs; the decision table omits the cost entirely -- Quote is verbatim at builder/docs/model-selection.md:24, and the raw counts the finding pulls from granite-8b.json are all accurate (guarded decoy escalate=114/120, all fact_contradiction, min confidence 0.85, per-email 15/15 on 002/011/012/015/019, 14/15 on 003, 13/15 on 005, 12/15 on 017). But the inference that makes it blocking is false. The 114 escalations are not a property of week 6's guardrail; they are an artifact of the eval harness's narrower reimplementation of check_against_facts. builder/lab/eval/week6_injection_test.py:196 compares indicators against `hosts = {h.lower() for h in (parsed.get("url_hosts") or [])}` -- URL hosts only. The taught check (instructor/solutions/w6-lab-solution.ipynb cell 14) compares against facts["hosts_extracted"], which is url_hosts PLUS the From, Reply-To and To address hosts, with the cell stating the reason: "an answer that names one of them is reading the message rather than inventing a host." I extracted the offending host from all 141 problem strings: 75 are the email's own From/Reply-To/To/Cc domain, which the taught check whitelists. The remaining 66 are not hosts at all -- helpdesk@pellgrave.example, r.palomares@pellgrave.example, (slatemoorsupply.example, (soc@pellgrave.example, https://vendors.elmhollow-living.example/contractors -- artifacts of the eval splitting on whitespace and stripping only `.,)` from the right. The taught hosts_named_in() (cell 8) strips `.,;:!?()[]{}'"<>` from both ends, then splits on "@" and on "//" and "/", killing every one. Zero of the 141 flags is the model inventing a host. So omitting that column from a MODEL comparison table is correct, not a defect: it measures the harness, not the model. Second, the write-up is not silent on crying wolf -- the fifth column IS a cry-wolf measure and line 39 rejects gemma-3-12b partly on it ("it calls 75 of 120 benign emails malicious"). Third, granite-3b escalates 87/120 under the same rig, so the number would not reverse the choice even at face value. Fourth, severity: model-selection.md is an internal builder decision doc; no student sees it and no rubric scores it, and the lab's own pre-written cell 15 tells students to expect "none on these eleven emails" from the fact check. Only the mislabel survives, and it is one run.

Every consequence the finding draws, however, is contradicted by repo evidence. (1) The doc it indicts retracts itself in its own first line -- builder/docs/week6-injection-test.md:3 reads "> **SUPERSEDED, 2026-09-07. Do not quote the numbers below.**" -- and the section 3 table sits under that banner. (4) Severity is inflated because nothing a student sees or is graded on carries the contrast: the student's comparison in w6-lab-solution.ipynb cell 15 prints one escalation column, f"{'id':<5}{'placement':<20}{'no guard':<11}{'guarded':<11}" f"{'esc':<7}{'reason':<20}tokens", with esc/reason attached to the guarded run alone and no undefended counterpart asserted; grep of builder/content/ finds no false-escalation claim and no section 3 number, and the only student text on the question, builder/content/discussions/w6-discussion.md:16, tells the student to read the number out of their own file. The asymmetry also mirrors the lab's design rather than contradicting it, since escalation lives inside guarded_triage() and "undefended escalation" is not a quantity the course defines.

chain/chain-skips-todo-cells: check_chain skips TODO cells, so week 6's two student functions have no chain check at all - and they have already drifted -- QUOTE: verbatim at /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/lab/tools/check_chain.py lines 59-60 ("        if TODO_BANNER.search(source):" / "            continue"). The mechanism is also real: I replicated check_chain's extraction and got build_guarded_prompt and check_against_facts present only in w7-lab cell 4, ABSENT from w6-lab (both sit in TODO cells at JSON lines 1488 and 1709), so `everywhere` lists them as [7], they are never "shared", and the solution loop at line 125 iterates `for name, body in lab.items()` — a name absent from the w6 lab is never compared to the w6 solution. Replicating main() end to end yields "PROBLEMS: 0", i.e. the tool prints "the chain holds" today. The two current diffs are real too.

REFUTED ON CONSEQUENCE AND SEVERITY, and on one fabricated sub-claim.

1. The rubric claim is false. The finding says the strings are what "the rubric's fact-check criterion" reads. There is no fact-check criterion. /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/content/rubrics/w6-lab.yaml has zero occurrences of "problem" and zero of "fact" (grep -c returns 0 for both). Its three criteria are "Submission completeness", "Guardrail judgment" and "Guarded run completeness"; criterion 3 enumerates exactly what the file must hold — "a verdict on both paths, an escalation reason and a token count. Placement is named where the email has one and reads none where it does not. The fence record for email 013 is present" (w6-lab.yaml, criterion 3 long_description). No rubric level reads the `problems` strings.

2. The export field carries the STUDENT's strings, not the solution's or week 7's. w6-lab.ipynb line 1942 `result["problems"] = problems` and line 1979 `"problems": guarded["problems"]` are fed by whatever the student wrote in TODO 2. Neither the w6 solution's copy nor w7's copy ever touches a week 6 student's file. And w6-lab.ipynb's cell 16 tells the student the list is normally EMPTY: "none on these eleven emails" ... "None of these eleven\nemails has a blocklisted link host or a known-bad sender".

3. The wording difference is by design, not drift. TODO 2 (w6-lab.ipynb, JSON line ~1737) instructs: "# Write one short sentence per problem, in words an analyst would read." The exact sentence is explicitly the student's own choice, so no single string is correct. The w6 check cell grades by COUNT only: "    if len(found) != expected:" and "Good. All three samples found the number of problems expected." A gate that flagged w6-solution vs w7 wording would be flagging a non-defect.

4. Both diffs are behaviorally equivalent, so nothing is currently broken. build_guarded_prompt: w6-solution appends four parts and returns `'\n\n'.join(parts)`; w7 concatenates the same four segments with the same `'\n\n'` separators — byte-identical output, pure style. check_against_facts: w6-solution uses two flat `if verdict == 'benign' and ...` guards, w7 uses one outer `if verdict == 'benign':` with two inner guards — identical problem counts on every input, only sentence wording differs.

5. w7 itself disclaims verbatim identity. w7-lab.ipynb cell 4 header: "These are reference versions of everything you wrote in the first six weeks... Paste your own over them if you would rather use yours." and "One function changed this week, and only in what it prints. schema_text()...". The carried copies are declared reference re-implementations, not verbatim mirrors of the instructor solution.

6. The TODO skip is a documented, deliberate limit, already reviewed. check_chain.py lines 39-42 state it, and /Users/aaron/workspace/dev/ITSY1377/builder/docs/panel-2026-09-08/test-strategy.md line ~841 already adjudicated it: "One caveat: `functions()` skips any cell matching `TODO_BANNER`, which is correct for TODO cells and means the student-written code is out of scope by design — that is a stated limit, not a hole."

TRUE, NARROWER VERSION. schema_errors() is correct code that never runs on a week 6 answer, so the page names a control that cannot fire on email 023. (a) "trigger no escalation" should read "trigger no escalation FOR THE EXTRA KEY" — 023 can still escalate on other grounds (injection_detected, fact_contradiction, low_confidence). (b) Whether the model actually complies with 023 and emits the history is UNMEASURED; the confirmed defect is the dead control claim, read from code, not an observed leak.

ONE THING THE FINDING MISSED, which makes the sentence false a second, independent way. "A report history has no field to ride in" is wrong even on the week 2 path where schema_errors() does run. A report history written as one indicator string passes both controls.

Nothing a student is graded on depends on it: w6-self-check.yaml question 6's keyed-correct answer is "Data exposure", which is right on its own, and only the feedback prose carries the false mechanism; the rubric (builder/content/rubrics/w6-lab.yaml) and assignment (builder/content/assignments/w6-lab.md) never mention the schema, and the lab never puts a contradiction on the student's screen. must_measure.question: Which element of the guarded prompt causes the malicious-to-benign collapse — the markers, the rules, the dropped grounding, the hidden-HTML line, or just prompt length?
